description:
The usa.gdt dataset is open in Gretl. It contains real US quarterly macroeconomic data from the Federal Reserve FRED database (1984Q1 to 2009Q3) with two variables: 'gdp' (real GDP in billions of chained 2005 dollars) and 'inf' (CPI inflation rate, annualized %).

Run an Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) unit root test on the 'gdp' variable to test whether GDP has a unit root (is non-stationary). In the main window, click on 'gdp' to select it, then use the menu: Variable > Unit root tests > Augmented Dickey-Fuller test. In the dialog, keep the default settings and click OK. When the results appear showing the ADF test statistic and critical values, save them to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/adf_test_results.txt using File > Save to file in the results window.

metadata.data_source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED database, via Hill et al. POE5
